why: It holds the April Fools frame: whether a sub's talk, a call included, is meant. It settles how talk is read for a day, not who does which part of the work or why.
remainder: change of level: it frames the setting the organization works in, which the four problems take as given

why: The host sub draws a line around canvas talk to protect its ordinary life. A megathread does channel information, but as a by-product of guarding the sub's boundary, which is what the acts are for.
remainder: change of level: it draws the boundary of the organization, which the frame's definition presupposes (identifiable boundaries)

why: Explaining what the canvas is, reading the finished picture and remarking on neighbours give members what they need to know to place a first pixel and read their corner.
cannot_do: No one holds the information to give. The account is pieced together from guesses about a new object, and it reaches only those who read the thread.

why: Carrying in the sub's quarrel, its lore, its ideology and its jokes tells the event in the room's frames: who the room is, not how its work is divided, assigned, paid or informed.
remainder: change of level: membership and meaning, the boundary the frame presupposes

why: By construction: its declaration says no one can hold a member's minutes or allocate them. A call offers a task, and whoever answers takes it: allocation by self-selection (Puranam, Alexy and Reitzig 2014, p. 171).
cannot_do: No one can assign a member to a task or hold one to it. The call only offers, and a room with no answers has no one to allocate.

why: It settles what the room will show of itself and so what it will act on: it makes the goal, which the four problems take as given.
remainder: different mechanism: making the goal (inheriting the topic's picture, arguing its design, adopting a mark found placed)

why: Members report the state of the mark to the thread: what is placed, done or missing, and where; the work and the reports on it are its own representation (Puranam, Alexy and Reitzig 2014, p. 172).
cannot_do: No one can tell a placer which pixel is theirs. The canvas shows anyone what is missing, attackers included, and it cannot say which version of the picture is meant.
was_why: The half-built mark tells the next placer what is missing and where; the work is its own representation (Puranam, Alexy and Reitzig 2014, p. 172).
amended: C5c-02: Stigmergy keeps building and reporting the mark alone (F-018); the mapping now rests on members' reports of the work's state

why: A template or coordinates map the picture into pixel-by-pixel tasks. That is the artifact that captures task division in the frame's own examples, like a workflow diagram or an engineering drawing (Puranam, Alexy and Reitzig 2014, p. 165).
cannot_do: No one can make a placer follow the template. It divides the work without assigning any part, and a rival can copy the same division to attack it.

why: Scripts, spare accounts and bots let a room place faster than its members can under the rate limit. They change how many hands there are, not how the work is divided, assigned, paid or informed.
remainder: different mechanism: multiplying the hands under a fixed rate, a change in the technology of production

why: Moving planning into a chat enriches the channel through which members coordinate, the frame's second route to information provision (Puranam, Alexy and Reitzig 2014, p. 166).
cannot_do: A chat's decisions bind no one outside it, and they reach the public thread only as announcements, so the members who never join it get the plan late or not at all.

why: Putting one member in charge, holding elections, dividing the picture among teams and handing the work over are allocation by decision: a member, a vote or a body assigns the parts and the offices.
cannot_do: A decided leader or team binds no placer who does not choose to follow. The allocation holds only as long as members keep accepting it, and it appears in 46 of 705 rooms.

why: Judging whether the room has the hands and the room for its work, urging others to give up and quitting under strain weigh whether the goal can be met. They do not divide, assign, pay or inform.
remainder: different mechanism: sizing or abandoning the goal, a judgment the frame leaves out because it assumes the goal

why: Watching, repairing, defending and reshaping the mark are the work itself, done again. Covering the night shift is allocation by who is awake, but it is one member of six.
remainder: change of level: the task beneath the problems of organizing it

why: Claiming, granting, yielding and abandoning a spot divide space between rooms, not tasks among members. A host vetting guests rules on other organizations' entry.
remainder: change of level: between organizations (space on a shared surface)

why: Sparing neighbours, reining in attackers and apologising keep rooms from harming each other's work. That is order between organizations, not within one.
remainder: change of level: between organizations (restraint without agreement)

why: Borders, truces, envoys and holding rooms to deals are explicit order made between rooms that cannot bind their own placers.
remainder: change of level: between organizations (negotiated order)

why: Helping other rooms, asking them for help, thanking allies and bartering help. At the level of rooms it resembles allocation and reward, but no member is assigned or paid.
remainder: change of level: between organizations; a renamed instance of allocation and reward one level up, with rooms in the place of members

why: Gathering kindred rooms, tallying their works, making joint marks and forming alliances organize rooms into bodies of rooms.
remainder: change of level: an organization of organizations

why: Tracing who changed the work, and telling vandalism from friendly work, give the room what it needs to know to answer a change.
cannot_do: The record does not show members seeing who placed a pixel. Members infer the author from the change, and they mistake friendly work for vandalism in 46 rooms.
amended: C5a-01: the first sentence stated a fact of the setting that the contract does not state (rule 14, after the declaration prose pass amended Attribution)

why: Defacing, encroaching, converting and griefing are the work turned against other rooms' works: moves in a contest, not ways of organizing one's own work.
remainder: change of level: between organizations (the contest)

why: Taunts, chants, victory claims and salutes carry a contest on in talk.
remainder: change of level: between organizations (the contest in talk)

why: Claiming the nation beyond the mark (kin, history, belonging, national others) says who the room is.
remainder: change of level: membership, the boundary the frame presupposes

why: Hailing a colour, professing loyalty, defecting and splitting over doctrine make and remake a faction the canvas grew.
remainder: change of level: membership made on the clock, the boundary the frame presupposes

why: Arguing over symbols, covering hate symbols and shutting down bigotry draw a moral line about what may stand.
remainder: change of level: the boundary of what the organization will carry

why: Members say being seen brought the room newcomers, returning fans, the creators' notice and press coverage; I read these as the room's return for the work.
cannot_do: No member of the room gives or withholds it. It comes from people outside the room, goes to the room rather than to a member, and in 3 rooms members say they fear the newcomers it brings.
amended: C5a-01: 'the whole site pays the room back' and 'an audience the room does not choose' were universal or figurative and no count supports them (rule 14, after the declaration prose pass amended Visibility returns)

why: By my reading, no longer by construction: since C5a-01 the declaration no longer says that the ritual pays members. Members credit who made the work (156 rooms), report their own parts (60) and hand out prizes (7); these map nonmonetary rewards to members, which the frame allows (Puranam, Alexy and Reitzig 2014, p. 165). Celebrating the finished work (442 rooms) maps nothing to anyone.
cannot_do: No one can pay, promote or withhold. Credit is given in words by peers, after the work, to anyone who claims a part, so it can induce only by expectation.
amended: C5a-01: the declaration prose pass removed 'the ritual pays the members whom no one could pay', on which the by-construction mapping rested; the mapping stays reward, by reading (rule 14)

why: Mourning, reporting how the work fared, saving timelapses and entering the work in atlases record what the work was after the clock.
remainder: change of level: the work's afterlife, after the organizing it records

why: Carrying the work to new canvases, repurposing the sub and proposing ties beyond the canvas are the forms that outlive the clock.
remainder: change of level: what outlives the organization, a new goal for a later one
